speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Welcome to Tirharad, traveller. Before I send you out there, show me what you can do. North of the square stand our training dummies. Use your abilities on three of them. Tab selects a target, and the number keys use your abilities.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The dummies are just north of the square. Keep swinging.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Not bad at all. You will be a credit to the Watch yet. Take this for your trouble.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Wolf pups have been wandering out of the north meadow, and the shepherds are afraid to leave their flocks. They are small, but they bite. Thin them out before they grow into something worse.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The meadow lies north of the village. Pups hunt in packs, so mind your health.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The shepherds can sleep tonight. Here, a charm made of pup teeth. It is not much, but it is honest work.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: Good leather is hard to come by since the wolves came down from the hills. Bring me four fresh pelts from the wolves east and north of the village, and I will make it worth your while.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: Four fresh pelts. Wolves along the East Road and in the meadow carry them.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: Fine pelts! I will have these cured by morning. Take this. I made it myself.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: Raiders have set up on the south road. They rob farmers, steal lambs and frighten travellers. The Watch is too thin to hunt them. Could you?

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: The raiders hide along the south road.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: The farmers can use the road again. Here, something for the trouble.

speaker: Merchant Brage
text: The raiders took my satchels, and my best wares were in them. If you find any, bring them to me. I will pay properly.

speaker: Merchant Brage
text: The raiders carry the satchels.

speaker: Merchant Brage
text: My goods! A little worse for the wear, but mine. Take this, and my thanks.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Wargs have made camp in the east, in the old stones by the mere. A warg does not make camp without a master, and this master is drawing them in. Find the camp, and see what it is hiding.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The warg camp lies south-east of Tirharad, across the mere.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: So many wargs, and orc-tracks everywhere. There is a war-band in the old tower, and it is feeding on this. We must act.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: The wargs are led by a great alpha the farmers call Shadowfang. Slay it, and the pack will scatter. It will not be easy. It never is.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: Shadowfang prowls the heart of the warg camp.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: Shadowfang is dead. The pack is broken. Tirharad can breathe, for a while.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Ostirith was our watchtower, once. Now orcs burn fires in its windows, and I have counted them every night. I want to know what they are doing. Scout the tower, and kill whoever stands in the way.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Ostirith lies in the far east of the Southlands, beyond the mere.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: An orc war-band, and they are not just raiding. They are fortifying. Someone is giving them orders.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The orcs carry tokens marked with a black hand, a sign of command. Bring me five, and I will know who orders them. Gather them from the tower, and be careful.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The orcs of Ostirith carry the tokens.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The black hand. Adar. I have heard that name whispered by prisoners. He is a leader of orcs, and he is not stupid. This is more than a raid.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: The spiders of the tower hold a venom that Torvald can use to temper blades. It is dangerous work. But a Watch that cannot fight is not much of a Watch.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: The spiders hide in the rubble of Ostirith.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: A fine venom. I will have blades that bite twice by evening. Take this.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: The tokens carry one name: Gorthak. He rules Ostirith from the old hall at the north end of the courtyard, and his war-band grows by the week. If he is not stopped, Tirharad will burn before winter. Take your company, and break him. Expect fire, and do not stand still when the ground glows.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Gorthak waits in the Warlord's Hall, at the northern end of Ostirith.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Ostirith is silent. You and your company did what a hundred soldiers could not. Tirharad will remember it, though the name they tell is unlikely to be yours. Take this, it is the least we can give.

speaker: Sadoc Burrows
text: Hullo there, little one. The caravan moves at first frost, and wolf pups from the hills have been snapping at the stragglers. Harfoots do not fight. But we do not leave anyone behind, either. Thin them out before the next camp?

speaker: Sadoc Burrows
text: The pups run in the hills north-east of the camp.

speaker: Sadoc Burrows
text: Quieter nights, and the little ones sleep at last. Here, a bit of bread. You look thin.

speaker: Largo Brandyfoot
text: The wolves ran off with the foraging baskets. Poppy's whole week of mushrooms and berries, gone. A Harfoot without a larder is a hungry Harfoot. Bring back what you can find, and I shall be in your debt.

speaker: Largo Brandyfoot
text: The baskets lie among the wolves in the hills and along the trail.

speaker: Largo Brandyfoot
text: My berries! Only a little chewed. You have done a good turn today, and I will say so around the fire.

speaker: Poppy Proudfellow
text: Tall folk, in dark hoods, asking after something that fell from the sky. They did not look kind. They were rough with the old ones. Could you scare them off? I would not ask, only Sadoc says you are the sort who might.

speaker: Poppy Proudfellow
text: The hooded strangers lurk along the trail, east of the camp.

speaker: Poppy Proudfellow
text: They are gone, and nobody was hurt. The Stranger will want to know. He was uneasy all night.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The hooded ones carry a mark I almost remember: black cloth, stamped with a pale hand. Take three from them and bring them to me. I do not yet know what they mean, but I am afraid I will soon.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The raiders carry the marks.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: A pale hand on black. I have seen this in a dream, I think, of fire and ash. We must warn someone who can read such signs.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Go south, to the village of Tirharad, where a Silvan Watchwarden named Arondir guards the road against the dark. Tell him what you have seen: the sky-fire, the hooded hunters, the mark of the hand. You are not brave, little one, and you do not have to be. You only have to be quick.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Take the south road to Tirharad and find Captain Arondir.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The Harfoots send you? Then it is even worse than I feared. Come, sit, and tell me everything.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: The new galleries are infested. Spiderlings, hundreds of them, boiling out of cracks that were sealed for ages. My axes cannot be everywhere. Clear the upper halls, and the delvers may work in peace.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: The spiderlings nest in the Silver Galleries.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: The galleries are quiet. Not safe, but quiet. A dwarf can work in quiet.

speaker: Brô the Miner
text: The silver-vein is richer than we thought, but the spiderlings guard the best seams. Bring me four chunks of the pale ore. The Prince himself has asked for samples, and a dwarf does not disappoint his Prince.

speaker: Brô the Miner
text: The ore lies with the spiderlings and the goblins in the galleries.

speaker: Brô the Miner
text: Look at that gleam! It sings, when the hammer touches it. I have never held anything like it.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: Goblins have come up from below, and they came armed. That is no accident. Something is driving them from their holes. Drive them back, and let us see what chased them.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: The goblins prowl the Broken Gate.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: Armed, and afraid, and pointed north. I like none of it. Take this, and keep your eyes open.

speaker: Narvi the Lore-keeper
text: There is a sigil scratched into the goblins' gear: a single eye. I have read the old records, and I do not like what they say. Bring me three, and let me be wrong.

speaker: Narvi the Lore-keeper
text: The goblins carry the sigils.

speaker: Narvi the Lore-keeper
text: The Eye. It is as the oldest tales said. The Enemy has not died, only hidden. This must reach the Elves.

speaker: Prince Durin
text: Prince Durin cannot leave the halls, and the Elves have not seen what we have seen. You will go. There is a Watchwarden at Tirharad, in the Southlands, who guards the road the Enemy's servants will use. Take him this: the Eye is open, and the goblins flee north.

speaker: Prince Durin
text: Take the road south to Tirharad and find Captain Arondir.

speaker: Prince Durin
text: Durin sends word? Then the Dwarves have seen what I have seen. Sit, friend. We have much to talk about.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: The old trees along the harbour road have begun to whisper, and the words are wrong. Spiderlings, I think, nesting in the roots. The Havens have been peaceful for a very long time. Please help us keep it so.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: The spiderlings gather in the Webbed Vale.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: The trees are quiet again. Thank you. I will write a verse about it. A short one.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: Silver webs where no spiders have been for an age. I have walked these shores for centuries, and I have never seen the like. Clear the Vale, and tell me what else you find there.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: The Webbed Vale lies south-east of the Havens.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: Cleaner. Not clean. There are tracks I do not recognise. I will think on it.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: Someone has been taking the silver leaves that ward the northern trace. It is petty theft, but wards do not fail by accident. Bring back four, and we may learn who sent the thieves.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: The goblins carry the leaves, north of the Havens.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: The wards will hold, for now. Whoever sent the thieves wanted to know how our wards were made. That is the kind of thing a hunter wants.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: Wargs hunt the Northern Trace, scouts, not true hunters. Something sends them to watch the Havens. I want a few of them gone, and I want the High King to know why.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: The warg scouts prowl the road east of the Havens.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: Scouts, sent by a hunter we have not met. The High King must hear this, and so must Galadriel, if she is not already too far south.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: High King Gil-galad has asked for a messenger to carry these tidings south. Galadriel hunts a shadow there, and the Watchwarden Arondir keeps the road. Take them what you have seen, and tell them the Havens stand with them.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Take the road south to Tirharad and find Captain Arondir.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: The High King sends word? Then Lindon has not forgotten us. Come in, and tell me what you have seen.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The wolves came down from the cliffs of Andustar at the turn of the season, and they are not afraid of the harbour dogs. Clear the cliffs, and the herders will sleep.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The wolves hunt on the cliffs, north-east of the harbour.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Good. The herders will breathe again. Stay a while: there is more work for a steady hand.

speaker: Aldor the Farmer
text: Raiders burned the granaries along the coast and carried off the grain, every sack. The winter will be hard for the shipwrights. If you find what they took, bring it back. I do not ask for justice. Bread will do.

speaker: Aldor the Farmer
text: The raiders on the Coast Road carry the stolen grain.

speaker: Aldor the Farmer
text: Grain! Honest grain. We shall eat this winter after all. Bless you, stranger. Take this.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: These raiders cannot be farmers gone wrong. They are organised, well armed and paid. By whom, I do not know. Break them, and see what they carry. The Coast Road runs east from the harbour.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The raiders hold the Coast Road, east of the harbour.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Black wax on their orders, and a mark I do not know. Whoever pays them has a long reach, and a longer purse.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: A ship without a flag was seen off the Black Landing, and tracks lead from the beach: hoofprints, deeper than any horse should leave. Go and see for yourself. Wargs prowl the shore, so watch your back. I need to know whether what I fear is true.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Black Landing lies south-east of the Coast Road. Wargs prowl there.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: It is as I feared. Something was landed there at night, and it is not here for trade. Someone must carry word to the Southlands, and I cannot leave my ship.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Queen Míriel has ordered ships to the Southlands, and I am sending word ahead: a Watchwarden named Arondir holds the village of Tirharad against whatever is coming. Take him this: the Númenóreans are on the way. Trust no one on the road you do not know.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Take the road east to Tirharad and find Captain Arondir.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Elendil sends you? Then Númenor has heard. Come, sit, and tell me everything.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Four roads have brought four warnings to my door: from the Harfoots, from Khazad-dûm, from Lindon and from Númenor. They say the same thing in different words. There is only one person who can make sense of this, and she is here in Tirharad, this very week: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies, who has hunted the Enemy for a thousand years. Go and speak to her.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Galadriel waits by the well in the market square.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: So. Four warnings, from four peoples, and one shadow behind them all. I have waited long for this council, even if it is only the two of us, and a few brave friends. Yes. It is time to act.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Gorthak is dead, and Ostirith is silent, but a warlord does not act without orders. Search his hall at the north end of the courtyard: any map or letter, anything with a mark on it. Bring it to Galadriel. She will know how to read it.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Search Gorthak's hall at the north end of Ostirith.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: A map of the southern ranges, and orders marked with the black hand. Gorthak was only a hunter, set to dig. Adar's orcs are tunnelling toward the mountain the Southlanders call Orodruin. I do not know why. I intend to find out.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The Commander has gone ahead, and the great ones will follow her: Elrond, Celebrimbor, Durin of Khazad-dûm and the Númenórean captains. I cannot take you with them, for that road is theirs. But someone must walk behind them: clear what follows, cover what they leave, carry what they cannot. Bronwyn and the Wayfarers shadow the road a day behind. Join them. First, say farewell to Captain Arondir.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Say farewell to Captain Arondir. A soldier deserves a farewell.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Then it begins. You will not be in the songs, friend, and neither will I. The songs will be about the great ones, and the stones they leave behind will be yours to keep clean. Book I is finished. The Ashen Road waits.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The mountain Orodruin has begun to wake, and the sky east of Tirharad is the colour of old iron. Galadriel passed along the road three days ago, with the Númenórean captains behind her. Bronwyn and the Wayfarers hold the halt at the foot of the Ashen Hills: join them, and follow the road east. You are the rearguard. Do not try to be the story.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Take the ashen road out of Tirharad, past Ostirith, to the Wayfarers' Halt.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: You are in time. We are not the heroes of songs, and that is how it should be. Songs need people who quietly do the work behind them. Welcome to the Wayfarers.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Commander's trail still smells of her horses, and the Ash Wargs have been following it like bloodhounds. If they are still running the road when the other great ones come through, someone will die. Thin them out before they find our fires.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Ash Wargs hunt along the scorched road, east of the halt.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Fewer teeth in the dark now. Still, wargs hunt for a master. Whoever rides them is close.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: Orc hunters came out of the east with something under their cloaks: a scrap of black cloth, passed from hand to hand like a holy thing. Take a few from them. Bronwyn will want to see it. And be careful. The cloth is cold, and it does not burn.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: The Ash Orc Hunters patrol the slopes north of the road.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: It is cold! The scrap feels cold, even through the glove. I will not touch it again. Take it to Bronwyn.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The scraps are shadow-cloth, woven by hands I would rather not meet. The orcs have a camp on the old watchtower, the ruined tower on the summit of the Ashen Hills. The dead of the old watch still walk there, bound by the dark. Climb the hill. Clear them, so the Wayfarers can pass.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Climb the hill to the Cinder Crown and clear the shades.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The tower is quiet, for now. From the summit I saw the scorched stone where something stood, and a smear of black on the old floor. Whatever Adar is doing, it is real.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: An ash-wraith has been left to watch the hill. It is a lesser servant of the shadow, but no small enemy. As long as it holds the summit, no one can pass or camp. Take the whole company, and break it in the ruins of the watchtower. Do not look into its hood. Do not stand in the cold that follows it.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Ash-wraith waits in the ruins of the Fallen Watchtower, on the summit of the Ashen Hills.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: It is driven off, not destroyed. Things like that cannot be killed, not by us. But the way to Eregion is open now. Elrond asked for scouts willing to follow the great ones. Go to Ost-in-Edhil, and tell him the road behind them is clear.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Elrond, the Herald of the High King, has asked for scouts willing to walk a day behind the great ones. Take the road west along the Sirannon to Ost-in-Edhil, the city of the smiths. Tell him the road behind is clear, and that the Wayfarers stand ready.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Follow the road to Ost-in-Edhil and find Elrond.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Bronwyn sends you? Then the Wayfarers have not failed. The great gathering is soon. Come in, and rest while you can: you will not have many more soft beds.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion, is the finest smith of the Second Age, and he asks everyone who comes from the road what they saw. He is a veteran of the First Age, and he does not repeat himself. Go and tell him what you saw on the Ashen Hills.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Find Celebrimbor in the smithies of Ost-in-Edhil.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: The Ash-wraith, and the shadow-cloth. You faced it, you and the Wayfarers? Brave. Not wise, but brave. The great ones will not know what you did, and that is as it should be.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: There is a Dwarf-princess in the lower hall who has not stopped working since she arrived, and nobody has told her to rest. She is Princess Disa, wife of Prince Durin. Sit with her a little before the gathering. Some tasks are harder than any battle.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: Disa is in the lower hall of Ost-in-Edhil.

speaker: Celebrimbor, Lord of Eregion
text: Ah, a visitor. Do you know the stone-songs? No? Never mind. I have been carving, you see. Will you give Durin this little token? No, wait, he is in the Forge Hall already. Then you keep it, and look after him if you see him. The mountain is a hard master.

speaker: Disa, Princess of Khazad-dûm
text: The High King's gathering meets soon in the Forge Hall, and the Elves, the Dwarves and Men have all sent their finest. Elrond wants to speak to you, not as one at the table, but as one of those who follow. Go to him when you are ready.

speaker: Disa, Princess of Khazad-dûm
text: Speak to Elrond when you are ready.

speaker: Disa, Princess of Khazad-dûm
text: You are not one of the great ones, and no song will name you. But the road behind them must be kept open, and their friends must reach them if they call. That is a task worth doing. Book II is complete: you have broken the wraith on the Ashen Hills and brought word to Eregion. The road goes ever on.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: The gathering met last night, in the Forge Hall: Elves, Dwarves and Men around the one table, with a stranger at its edge. I was there, and I will tell you what was said. But first see the Hall for yourself: the empty chairs, the cold anvil and the fire still burning.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Enter the Forge Hall, in the heart of Ost-in-Edhil.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: It is decided. The mithril goes to the smiths, and the smiths will try to make something that has never been made. Rings, three of them for the Elves, seven for the Dwarves and nine for Men. Celebrimbor has spoken. We are the ones who follow.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Three have come to the forge whom you should know by sight: Isildur of Númenor, son of Elendil; Halbrand, a wanderer with a smith's hands who has barely spoken; and Durin, Prince of Khazad-dûm. You will walk where they walk, and it is good to know their faces. Speak to each, then tell Galadriel you will follow.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Isildur, Halbrand and Durin are in the courtyards of Ost-in-Edhil.

speaker: Elrond, Herald of Gil-galad
text: Good. Then you have seen them, and you will know them by their footprints. They leave at dusk. You will leave a day behind, and keep to their trail. I do not like that wanderer. I cannot tell why.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The mithril caravans have gone south and east, toward the Gate of Khazad-dûm, and the great ones follow. Take the road after them. The Wayfarers make camp where they camp. Their fires are cold now, but I would like to know what the ashes say.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Take the east road out of Ost-in-Edhil to the Mithril Road.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: The Mithril Road. They slept here, you see? The ring of stones where Durin's pipe was knocked out. Keep your blade out. The wolves that followed them are still around.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The wolves came after the caravans, as the wargs did on the ash road. They are lean and clever, and they are watching our camp now. Drive them off, and mind the old road: not everything that hunts here has fur.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Hollin Wolves roam the old road and the foothills east of camp.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Better. Not safe, but better. There is also the matter Mirieth has been muttering about.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: There are orcs on the old road wearing a mark: a burnt hand-print on every strap and satchel. These are not hunters. They belong to Adar, and they have been following the caravans since Ost-in-Edhil. Take a few of their brands. Bronwyn needs to see them, and I need to be wrong.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: Adar's Scouts patrol the old road and the way to the Gate.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: The black hand again, and burnt into everything. Adar is following the mithril. The great ones do not know. We must be their eyes.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: There are shadows on the old road, tall and cold, that were not here an age ago. A dwarf has little patience for ghosts, but a great deal for axes. Clear them out, so the Wayfarers may sleep, and I will tell my kin at Khazad-dûm that you helped.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: The Ashen Wights haunt the old elf-road.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: Hah! The dead stay dead, then, when properly reminded. Good work. I shall sing about it later, quietly, so as not to disturb the Wayfarers.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The road to the Gate of Khazad-dûm runs beside a black pool, and the pool is not empty. The caravans passed it, and it took a toll; now it is awake and hungry, and it will take a hand from anyone who follows. It must be dealt with before the Wayfarers can pass. Be fast, and do not stand in the water.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Deep Watcher waits in the Pool by the Gate, south-east of the old road.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The water is still. Not forever, I think, but long enough for us to reach the Gate. You have my thanks, and Khazad-dûm's soon enough.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Gate of Khazad-dûm is at the foot of the cliff, on the far side of the pool. Prince Durin opened it for the caravans, and it stands open still, to his friends. Nár is waiting by the Gate: he knows the old greeting of his people, and he will see us in.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Stand before the West Gate of Khazad-dûm, at the east end of the road.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Gate stands open, and Nár bows us in. I do not like the smell of what waits inside. Book III is done, and the mountain waits. Khazad-dûm is before us, and what we find there, none of us can say.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Gate is open, and there is no other way. The Redhorn is behind us, and the wolves are behind us. Under the mountain, and out the other side. Stay close, light no more than you need, and call out if you see anything that glows.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: Pass through the West Gate and into Khazad-dûm.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Gate has closed behind us. Well. That decides it. We go forward, following the road the great ones walked, and not all of them walked it unharmed.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: Goblins, a great many, and they are coming from the south hall. They are armed, and they are not afraid of dwarves. There is a vein I want to see, and I will not do it with goblin arrows in my back. Clear the hall. Let them hear what a dwarf sounds like when he is angry.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: Goblins infest the Hall of Pillars, east of the gate.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: Better. They will come back, they always do, but for now the hall is quiet. Here, take a drink. It is dwarf-brewed. Do not ask what is in it.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Dwarves keep a ledger of every vein they cut, and the Orcs have torn it apart. If we are to know where the mithril lies, and what the Orcs are afraid of, we need those pages. Search the fallen, and bring me whatever you can.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Orc Captains in the Hall of Pillars carry the pages.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: ...vein runs deeper than any soundings... drums, drums in the deep... they are coming. It is as I feared. Whatever sleeps beneath this mountain has woken, and it is not the Orcs they fear.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: The richest vein in Khazad-dûm, and the reason the Elves came. Durin passed it with the caravans, and I need to see it with my own eyes, even if the Orcs have been at it. It lies east of the great hall. Take the left passage, and keep your eyes open.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: The Mithril Vein lies east of the Hall of Pillars.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: ...There it is. A river of silver in the black rock, glowing like a field of stars. It is beautiful. And it is the cause of everything. I will remember this, and I hope the Dwarves will too.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: We have made too much noise. The drums are louder now, and there is a troll in the vein chamber, a great one, and he is not alone. It nearly broke the caravan guards. Break him. The way to the Bridge is through the chamber.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The troll waits in the Mithril Vein.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: He is down. Good. Now we move. The Bridge of Durin is east of here, and something is stirring beneath it.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: This is where the great ones crossed, and where the digging went deepest. Something woke below, something old, born of fire and shadow, and it has burned a hole in the heart of the mountain. The creature itself is bound, for now, but its ember clings to the broken bridge, and it will burn anyone who tries to cross. It must be put out. Do it for the caravans, and for those who follow.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The Bridge of Durin lies at the far east of Khazad-dûm. The ember of the Deep Shadow still burns there.

speaker: Bronwyn, Leader of the Wayfarers
text: The last ember is out. The Bridge is dark. Whatever the Dwarves dug up, it will not climb out tonight. Book IV is complete: you followed the great ones through Khazad-dûm and cleared the road behind them. The rings are being forged, the mithril is safe, and what comes next is for the great ones to tell. The tale of the Rings of Power continues.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Welcome to Tirharad. We hold this village against the dark, and we are fewer every week.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Orc-fires burn on the old tower. They gather there, and they are not idle.

speaker: Arondir, Watchwarden
text: Watch yourself out there. We will soon have need of someone like you.

speaker: Merchant Brage
text: Fair prices, honest weights. The orcs have not yet taken my coin, and I would like it to stay that way.

speaker: Merchant Brage
text: They say the wargs carry goods plundered from the road.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: A good blade is worth nothing without a hand that can wield it.

speaker: Smith Torvald
text: Bring me your gear when it needs tending. I mean to keep the Watch armed.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: The south gate is open, but do not venture out after dark.

speaker: Sentry Ulf
text: The roads are safe enough, if you keep to them.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: I have hunted a shadow for a thousand years. It does not rest, and so neither shall I.

speaker: Galadriel, Commander of the Northern Armies
text: Do not ask me to be gentle. Ask me to be right.

speaker: Sadoc Burrows
text: A caravan is only as quick as its slowest foot, and we leave no foot behind.

speaker: Sadoc Burrows
text: Keep to the shadows, little one. Harfoots do not make a fuss.

speaker: Poppy Proudfellow
text: There is always something good at the bottom of a berry basket, if you do not give up.

speaker: Poppy Proudfellow
text: Strange tall folk asking questions on the trail. I do not like it.

speaker: Largo Brandyfoot
text: A good Harfoot knows where the berries grow. A great one knows where the wolves do not.

speaker: Prince Durin
text: The mountain has more to give than we dare take. That is both its gift and its warning.

speaker: Prince Durin
text: Stone does not forget, and neither do I.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: Keep your axe sharp and your wits sharper.

speaker: Captain Ragni
text: Goblins do not scare a dwarf. They merely annoy him.

speaker: Narvi the Lore-keeper
text: I read the stars and the stones. Both speak of change, and not all of it is welcome.

speaker: Brô the Miner
text: Honest work, mining. Dark, but honest. And the silver-vein is nearer than ever.

speaker: Lindir the Minstrel
text: Do you hear it? The trees of the Havens are singing softly tonight, and the song is wrong.

speaker: Thalion, Warden of the Havens
text: I have watched these shores for centuries. The shadow was not this patient before.

speaker: Elrond, the Herald
text: The High King sees further than any of us. I merely carry his words, and try to understand them.

speaker: Captain Elendil
text: The sea has been strange this season, and so have the sails on it.

speaker: Captain Elendil
text: A captain does not choose his storms, only his ship.

speaker: Aldor the Farmer
text: My granary stood full at midsummer. Now there is not a sack left.

speaker: Scout Mirieth
text: I counted nine fires on the hill last night. Then I stopped counting.

speaker: Disa, Princess of Khazad-dûm
text: Dwarves are not afraid of the dark. We simply respect what lives in it.

speaker: Isildur of Númenor
text: My father says the sea keeps its secrets. I am less patient than he is.

speaker: Halbrand, the Wanderer
text: Everything can be forged into something better. That is the only lesson worth learning.

speaker: Durin IV, Prince of Khazad-dûm
text: Mithril. A metal that glows like starlight in the dark. We should be careful what we do with it.

speaker: Herald Calithil
text: Every message has a sender. Every sender has a motive. Remember both.

speaker: Nár the Delver
text: I know the Gate of Durin as I know my father's face. Something has changed in the stone, though.
